role.title: Roles
role.assignHint: Checking a parent also checks everything under it, and a half-checked parent directory code is granted on save too (otherwise the API stays open while the menu stays hidden). A row tagged 'this level only' is granted in the database with none of its children granted: it shows no checkmark, yet saving keeps it. Touching that row or anything under it drops that carry-over. Accounts under this role must sign in again for the change to take effect — if you belong to this role, saving signs you out too.
role.assignOrphans: {n} granted entries no longer exist in the permission catalogue; they are kept as-is on save instead of being cleaned up.
role.assignEmptyConfirm: Nothing is checked. Saving revokes all {n} permissions of this role. Continue?

dept.desc: Maintain this tenant's organisation tree; user profiles pick their department from here
dept.name: Department

config.title: Platform settings
config.mourningDesc: When on, the admin app, designer and public share pages render in greyscale

channel.title: Notify channels
channel.desc: Delivery channels for alert notifications; a rule looks up a channel by type and only one row per type is ever used
channel.listHint: Press Enter or comma to add more
channel.noSchema: The server reports no usable notify-channel implementations (/alert/channel/schema returned empty), so creating and testing are unavailable
channel.testRecipientsEmail: Inboxes for this test, comma separated
channel.testRecipientsMobile: Phone numbers for this test, comma separated
channel.testRecipientsNote: Leave it empty to use whatever real dispatch would resolve (the rule's notify groups, else the channel's stored recipients). Anything typed here is used once and never saved.

testSourceKind.channelConfig: the channel's stored recipients (legacy — move them to notify targets)
testSourceKind.none: nothing resolved (this test had no recipients)

channel.legacyRecipients: This config still carries historical recipient item(s): {keys}. Recipients are now set per rule under Alerts · Notify targets; these stored values only act as a fallback when a rule has no usable group. Set the people up on the notify-target page to retire them.
channel.testNote: A test send writes no notification log and raises no alert event; the result is only echoed here, and the message body says it is a connectivity test.
channel.notDeliverableHint: This channel's config can be saved and validated, but the server has no working sender for it yet, so real alerts end up logged as failures.
channel.shadowed: Another enabled row of this type: ID {id}
channel.shadowHint: Dispatch takes the enabled row with the smallest id per type, so this row is never used.
channel.secretKept: Stored (leave as-is to keep, clear and save to revoke)

contact.title: Notify targets · Contacts
contact.desc: The alert roster. A person is configured once, grouped, and rules reference the group — so changing recipients never means editing a channel
contact.name: Name
contact.reachableRequired: Provide at least an email or a mobile number
contact.reachableHint: Someone with no reachable address receives nothing even when added to a group
contact.deleteTip: This person is still in one or more notify groups, so deleting is refused. To stop their alerts, switch them to disabled — dispatch skips disabled contacts.
contact.emailInvalid: Not a valid email address (like ops@example.com)
contact.mobileInvalid: Not a valid mobile number: 5-20 digits, optional + country code

notifyGroup.title: Notify targets · Groups
notifyGroup.desc: Bundle contacts into a group; rules reference the group to decide who gets this alert
notifyGroup.name: Group name
notifyGroup.memberEmpty: No members yet: an alert on this group reaches nobody
notifyGroup.unreachableWarning: This group has no deliverable address right now: nobody in it, or everyone is disabled. Rules pointing at it will notify nobody.
notifyGroup.deleteTip: Rules still reference this group, so deleting is refused. To pause its alerts, disable the group instead.
notifyGroup.disabledTip: Once a group is disabled, rules referencing it resolve nobody from it and fall back to the channel's stored recipients, if any.

permRule.title: Data permission rules
permRule.desc: Restrict which rows a user or role can query and which columns they can see; datasets without an enabled rule are untouched
permRule.name: Rule name
permRule.namePlaceholder: e.g. Sales sees own department only
permRule.datasetHint: Leave empty to apply this rule to every dataset in the tenant
permRule.conditionsHint: Conditions inside one rule are AND'ed, rules are OR'ed. Leave empty to hide columns only. Values can be placeholders (:userId etc); the rule is rendered once on save to prove it works
permRule.listValueHint: Values, press Enter to add; placeholders allowed
permRule.listRequired: In / Not in needs at least one value
permRule.betweenHint: Two bounds, press Enter to add; placeholders allowed
permRule.restrictedColumnsPlaceholder: Pick or type column names to hide
permRule.restrictedColumnsHint: These columns are removed from results. A query that references one is rejected instead of silently losing the column
permRule.atLeastOne: Provide row conditions or hidden columns, otherwise this rule does nothing
permRule.explainDesc: Compute with the current account: which rules hit, what row predicate is rendered, which columns are hidden
permRule.explainDenyAll: This account would get no rows
permRule.explainDenyAllTip: The dataset has enabled rules but this account matches none of them, so queries return an empty set rather than everything.
permRule.explainNoRule: No enabled rule on this dataset, queries stay unrestricted

license.title: License
license.notActivatedTip: Activation needs the signing secret on the server (LICENSE_SECRET env var); without it activation fails loudly instead of falling back to a built-in key.
license.expiredTip: This license is now history: activating a new one keeps this row as a record instead of overwriting it.
license.activateTip: The key is only verified server-side; the database stores its fingerprint (first 6 bytes of sha256) and never returns the key

audit.title: Audit log
audit.desc: Full trace of platform administration operations

schedule.title: Scheduled jobs
schedule.desc: The server runs registered handlers on a cron cycle; the outcome lives in the log, not on the button
schedule.cronHint: Spring 6-field form: second minute hour day month weekday. A wrong field count or mixed wildcards is rejected on save.
schedule.riskUnregistered: Every trigger of this job writes one failure line: the handler it points at is not registered on the server. Edit it to choose an available handler, or delete it.
schedule.noHandlerTitle: No handler is registered on the server
schedule.noHandlerDesc: Schedulable handlers are a closed set registered server side, not a free-text field here. This build ships one handler that prunes job logs; if the list is empty, schedule-service was not rebuilt - rebuild and restart port 8095.
schedule.noHandlerInForm: No handler to pick: candidates come from the server registry and cannot be typed in.
schedule.paramsNotJson: Parameters are not valid JSON. The handler receives this text verbatim, so a parse error is one failed run.
schedule.misfireHint: This field is only stored; the scheduler never reads it. Runs missed while the service was down are neither replayed nor made up once. Treat it as an operations note, not system behaviour.
schedule.pausedEditTip: This job is not running: saving a new cron does not arm a trigger. Use Resume to schedule it again.
schedule.runOnceQueued: A run has been queued: check the log for the result, this message does not mean it succeeded.
schedule.logsExplain: Every trigger leaves one row: success says what ran, failure says why it did not. Run now goes down the same path.

monitor.title: Service monitor
monitor.desc: Registered service instances, health summary and current metric values; the data comes from each service own registration and heartbeat
monitor.emptyDesc: The instance list is empty, which means nobody has called the registration endpoint - it does not mean every service is down. The expected caller of registration, heartbeat and metric reporting is the service process itself, and neither this backend nor the frontend calls it today, so this page will most likely stay empty. To fill it, services need self-registration first.
monitor.staleTitle: Statuses lag: the monitor sweeps every 30 seconds and marks an instance dead only after 90 seconds without a heartbeat, so what you see is not a live reading.
monitor.metricsNowHint: Only the latest row per instance and metric name; for curves open the history.
monitor.noMetrics: This service has not reported metrics
monitor.historyNote: Empty when nothing was reported: metrics also come from the services own reporting endpoint.

openPlatform.title: Open platform
openPlatform.desc: Outbound credentials and callback URLs: the two credential surfaces follow different rules, this page fills each by its own
openPlatform.secretOnceHint: A client secret is returned only on mint or reset; no later endpoint gives it back - copy and store it now.
openPlatform.rateLimitHint: Requests per minute. The server counts them; leaving this empty stores 60.
openPlatform.allowedIpsPlaceholder: One per line, or comma separated
openPlatform.allowedIpsHint: Leave empty to allow any source.
openPlatform.resetConfirm: Resetting the secret of {name} invalidates the old one immediately; every caller still using it starts returning 401 at once. Continue?
openPlatform.secretTitle: Credential generated, shown this time only
openPlatform.secretOnceWarning: Once this dialog is closed the secret is gone; the only way to see it again is to reset it.
openPlatform.copyFailed: The browser refused clipboard writes: select and copy manually. After closing this dialog the secret is not visible again.
openPlatform.disableConfirm: After disabling, the secret of {name} can no longer call open endpoints.
openPlatform.disabledNoEnable: Disabled (the server has no re-enable endpoint)
openPlatform.appSecretExposedTitle: This surface returns App Secret in the list and detail responses (existing backend behaviour)
openPlatform.appSecretExposedDesc: The client surface never echoes it; it is handed out once on mint or reset. The difference is not a frontend choice: AppVO in openapi-service carries an appSecret field. Values are masked by default here, use Show to reveal.
openPlatform.permissionsHint: This string is only recorded on the app; the verification path does not read it today, so filling it in changes nothing about what the app may call.
openPlatform.ipWhitelistHint: On the app surface this is a plain string field (the client surface uses an array); leave empty to allow any source.
openPlatform.secretRegenerated: A new secret has been generated
openPlatform.urlPattern: Must be a full URL starting with http(s)://
openPlatform.signSecretPlaceholder: Type your own; used to sign the callback body
openPlatform.signSecretHint: You supply it and it is stored as-is; the server signs callbacks with it.
openPlatform.webhookNote: This registers where the server would send. No event dispatcher calls these URLs yet, so the list is a configuration register, not evidence that a callback was delivered.

approval.title: Approval center
approval.desc: The trail and the decision for publish approvals
approval.commentSharedColumn: The note and the application reason share one column: writing here overwrites what the applicant entered.
approval.noAutoPublish: A decision only changes the status of this ticket: approving does not publish the screen or dashboard and does not notify the applicant. Publishing still happens in the designer.

file.title: File management
file.desc: Objects already stored in file-service. Upload and delete need file:write; images have a separate public read path for dashboards.
file.publicNote: /view/{id} only serves image/* without a session token; download needs login and file:read.
file.name: File name
file.confirmDeleteRow: Delete "{name}"? The physical file goes with it, and a deleted background image blanks the dashboard.
